Health data privacy policy

Version of November 23, 2026. There are no earlier versions.

This is Baseline’s consumer health data privacy policy. It covers the health data Baseline collects and why, who handles it, how long it’s kept, and how you can download it, delete it or withdraw your agreement. Baseline is run by [name of the person or business responsible for Baseline].

In short

  • Baseline stores the weights, measurements and notes you enter so it can show your trend.
  • It never sells your data or uses it for ads, and has no analytics or trackers.
  • Four services handle data for Baseline: Vercel, Neon, Clerk and, for reminders, your browser’s push service.
  • You can download your data or delete it at any time, in Your data.
  • Nothing is saved until you agree to this policy, and withdrawing your agreement deletes your data.

What Baseline collects, and why

Weigh-ins
The date and weight of each weigh-in, and any note you add, for your 14-day average, weekly trend, chart, forecasts and monthly summary. A note is whatever you type, so it can say something about your health. Write only what you want kept.
Height
For your BMI.
Waist measurements
Each waist measurement, and whether the male or female formula applies, for your body fat estimate. Baseline asks which formula to use only when you log a waist.
Your goal
Your goal weight, start date and start weight, an optional target rate and the number of milestones, for your progress and forecasts.
Your settings
Your units, and whether the overview shows BMI and body fat.
Reminders
If you turn them on: the hour, your time zone, and a push address for each device that gets them, so Baseline can send a reminder on days you haven’t weighed in.
Your agreement
Which version of this policy you agreed to, and when.
Your account
Your email address and, if you sign in with Google, your name and profile picture. Clerk, which runs sign-in, also records your sign-ins, such as the time, browser and IP address.

Baseline works out your averages, trend, BMI, body fat and forecasts in your browser each time it shows them, and doesn’t store them.

Where it comes from

Only from you. Baseline doesn’t get health data from anyone else, and doesn’t buy data. If you sign in with Google, Google gives Clerk your name, email address and profile picture.

What Baseline doesn’t collect

  • No analytics, advertising or tracking code runs on Baseline’s pages. The only code on them that isn’t Baseline’s own is Clerk’s sign-in, which can add a bot check from Cloudflare when you sign up.
  • Baseline sets no cookies of its own. Clerk sets cookies that keep you signed in, and they aren’t used for tracking or ads.
  • Baseline never asks for your location. The time zone saved with a reminder is the only clue it keeps to where you are, though the IP addresses that Vercel and Clerk record can show roughly where a request came from.
  • Baseline reads nothing from other apps, your contacts, your photos or your device’s sensors.

Who handles it

These services handle data so that Baseline can work. None of them gets more than the description says.

Vercel
Hosts Baseline’s pages and runs its server, which is in the United States. Vercel sees every request, with your IP address and browser. The server writes its errors to Vercel’s logs, and an error from the database can include the value it was saving, such as a weight. Vercel keeps these logs for up to a day.
Neon
Hosts Baseline’s database in the United States. It holds everything under “What Baseline collects” except your account, and encrypts it on disk. Neon is part of Databricks.
Clerk
Runs sign-in and keeps your account. Its sign-in form and account menu run on Baseline’s pages. Baseline sends none of your health data to Clerk. Clerk is based in the United States.
Push services
Only if you turn reminders on. Your browser’s push service delivers them: Apple for Safari, Microsoft for Edge, Mozilla for Firefox, and Google for Chrome and most other browsers. Each reminder is encrypted for your device, so the service can’t read it. It does see when one is sent, which can show that you hadn’t weighed in that day.
Google
Only if you sign in with Google. Google knows you signed in to Baseline, and gets none of your health data.

Baseline shares your data with no one else. It never sells your data and never uses it for ads.

How long it’s kept

Your log, settings and agreement
Until you delete them, your data or your account. Baseline doesn’t delete accounts that go unused.
Reminder devices
Until you turn reminders off or delete your data, or the push service ends the device’s subscription.
Your account at Clerk
Until you delete your account.
Server logs at Vercel
Up to a day.
Neon’s restore history
Neon keeps a history of every change, so the database can be put back as it was after a mistake. Deleted data stays in that history for up to 6 hours, and then it’s gone. If the database is ever restored, Neon keeps a copy from before the restore, and Baseline deletes that copy within 7 days. Baseline makes no other backups.
On your device
Baseline keeps a copy of your log and any changes waiting to sync in your browser, so it opens offline. Signing out, or deleting your data on that device, removes them.

Your choices

Baseline gives everyone these choices, wherever they live. Most of them are in Your data, linked from Settings and from the bottom of Baseline’s pages.

Download
Download weigh-ins (CSV) saves your weigh-ins for a spreadsheet. Download everything (JSON) saves everything under “What Baseline collects” except your account and your devices’ push addresses.
Correct
Edit any weigh-in, waist measurement, goal or height in Baseline, and delete any weigh-in, waist measurement or goal. Change your email address in Manage account, in Settings.
Delete
Delete my data deletes your log and keeps your account. Delete my account deletes your log and then your account. Either takes effect on the server at once, and leaves your data only in Neon’s restore history, for up to 6 hours. Your other devices drop their copy the next time they load your log.
Withdraw your agreement
Withdraw, in Your data, deletes your log as Delete my data does, because Baseline keeps health data only with your agreement. Baseline then saves nothing new until you agree again.
Ask
To ask what Baseline holds about you and who has received it, for a copy, or about anything in this policy, email [contact email address]. Baseline answers within one month, at no charge.
Appeal
If Baseline turns down a request, reply to its answer with “Appeal” in the subject. Baseline answers an appeal within one month.
Complain
You can also complain to the data protection authority or attorney general where you live.

Keeping it safe

Baseline’s pages and server talk over encrypted connections. The server answers only requests that carry your Clerk sign-in, and reads and writes only your own log. If your data is ever exposed in a breach, Baseline will tell you.

Changes to this policy

When this policy changes, the date at the top changes too. If a change affects what Baseline does with your health data, Baseline asks you to agree again before it saves anything new.
